sentences.zh: 从学术界进入工业界工作是什么感觉？

sentences.en: Well, they're both, they're both working.
sentences.zh: 嗯，它们其实都是在工作。

sentences.en: But what's it like to go from working at a university or studying at a university to a full-time job?
sentences.zh: 但从大学学习或工作环境转到全职工作是什么感觉？

sentences.en: Maybe I should answer this because you went straight from elementary school to working, right?
sentences.zh: 也许我应该回答这个问题，因为你是直接从小学毕业就去工作了，对吧？

sentences.en: I did have a job for most of high school and college, a full-time job.
sentences.zh: 我在高中和大学的大部分时间里确实有一份全职工作。

sentences.en: Anyways, so, yeah.
sentences.zh: 总之，是这样。

sentences.en: Well, yeah, you go first, and then I'll try.
sentences.zh: 好吧，你先说，然后我再试着回答。

sentences.en: Okay.

sentences.en: So for me, I only did undergraduate, so four years of college.
sentences.zh: 对我来说，我只读了本科，也就是四年大学。

sentences.en: So I'm not an academic, long-term student.

sentences.en: Well, you did a master's, right?
sentences.zh: 嗯，你读了硕士，对吧？

sentences.en: Well, I did a master's while I was working, so.
sentences.zh: 我是边工作边读的硕士，所以……

sentences.en: Oh, I see.
sentences.zh: 哦，我明白了。

sentences.en: So you kind of did, yeah, that makes sense.
sentences.zh: 所以你算是……嗯，这说得通。

sentences.en: So I'd already started working.
sentences.zh: 所以我当时已经开始工作了。

sentences.en: And I had an internship, actually, after my second year of school.
sentences.zh: 而且我在大二之后其实还做过实习。

sentences.en: So I went to school for two years, and I had already worked.
sentences.zh: 所以我读了两年书，就已经开始工作了。

sentences.en: And I think that eased some of it.
sentences.zh: 我觉得这减轻了一些过渡的压力。

sentences.en: So I recommend internships are a really good thing.
sentences.zh: 所以我推荐实习，这真的是件好事。

sentences.en: Oh, definitely.
sentences.zh: 哦，绝对的。

sentences.en: Because engineering internships are almost always paid.
sentences.zh: 因为工程类实习几乎都是有薪水的。

sentences.en: I've never heard of an unpaid engineering internship.
sentences.zh: 我从没听说过无薪的工程实习。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And so you get money.
sentences.zh: 所以你还能赚到钱。

sentences.en: That's cool.
sentences.zh: 那很酷。

sentences.en: And then also, like, it does expose you for, like, you know, going back to school for the remainder of the time to, like, know what to study and what you're interested in and
sentences.zh: 而且，这也能让你在剩下的求学期间，知道自己该学什么，对什么感兴趣，以及……

sentences.en: what the real life, I'm doing little quotes here, is all about.
sentences.zh: 所谓的“现实生活”（我这里打个引号）到底是什么样的。

sentences.en: But, I mean, I think the biggest transition is from the fact that, like, in academic, it's perfectly to say things like always and never.
sentences.zh: 但我认为最大的转变在于，在学术界，说“总是”和“从不”这类绝对的话是完全没问题的。

sentences.en: And in real life, you can't really say those things because you have to bend or break a lot of rules because you may be working on older technology or, like, the style of your team
sentences.zh: 但在现实生活中，你不能那样说，因为你必须变通或打破很多规则，因为你可能是在使用旧技术，或者你们团队的风格……

sentences.en: is just this.
sentences.zh: 就是这样。

sentences.en: And even though academically, you may be able to show, like, this paper says this is the more optimal way to do this.
sentences.zh: 即使在学术上，你可能证明了某篇论文说这是最优解。

sentences.en: It's like, well, we already have coded this.
sentences.zh: 但现实是，我们已经写好代码了。

sentences.en: We've already invested the time and tested it and, you know, whatever.
sentences.zh: 我们已经投入了时间、进行了测试，诸如此类。

sentences.en: Yeah, that's a good point.
sentences.zh: 是的，这是一个很好的观点。

sentences.en: You know, like, we were talking about this today at lunch that, you know, in Python, in the Python compiler, there's something called TimSort.
sentences.zh: 你知道，就像我们今天午餐时谈到的，Python 编译器里有一种叫 TimSort 的算法。

sentences.en: And it's named after Tim.
sentences.zh: 它是以 Tim 的名字命名的。

sentences.en: And the idea is, you know, they need to do some kind of sorting.
sentences.zh: 思路是，他们需要进行某种排序。

sentences.en: And again, I'm not going to go into the details.
sentences.zh: 我不会深入细节。

sentences.en: I don't even really know the details, but to some extent, part of the Python compiler needed to sort something.
sentences.zh: 我甚至不太了解细节，但在某种程度上，Python 编译器的一部分需要对某些东西进行排序。

sentences.en: But they knew something about the data.
sentences.zh: 但他们对数据有所了解。

sentences.en: Like, they knew certain chunks of the data were already in some kind of order.
sentences.zh: 比如，他们知道数据的某些部分已经是有序的了。

sentences.en: And so TimSort, you know, took advantage of some of the assumptions they could make about the data to sort faster than n log n.
sentences.zh: 所以 TimSort 利用了他们对数据所做的假设，从而实现了比 n log n 更快的排序。

sentences.en: Right, which, just to recap, like, if you take computer science 101, one of the first things
sentences.zh: 没错，回顾一下，如果你上过计算机科学 101，你学到的第一件事就是……

sentences.en: you'll learn is that, you know, the two fastest sorts, theoretically, QuickSort and MergeSort, both run in n log n.
sentences.zh: 理论上最快的两种排序算法，快速排序和归并排序，运行时间都是 n log n。

sentences.en: But TimSort, you know, given the data that TimSort works on, runs in faster than n log n.
sentences.zh: 但 TimSort 在处理它所针对的数据时，运行速度比 n log n 快。

sentences.en: And so the point is, you know, when you get down to industry, you're not working on, like, theoretically, theoretical data.
sentences.zh: 所以重点是，当你进入工业界时，你处理的不是理论上的数据。

sentences.en: I mean, you're working on practical data that you can make a lot more assumptions on.
sentences.zh: 你处理的是实际数据，你可以对其做出更多的假设。

sentences.en: And so a lot of the theory kind of goes out the window.
sentences.zh: 所以很多理论在现实中就没那么适用了。

sentences.en: Yep.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: That's my biggest thing.
sentences.zh: 这是我最大的感触。

sentences.en: I don't know.
sentences.zh: 我不知道。

sentences.en: Yeah, I guess my biggest thing is, I kind of look at it this way.
sentences.zh: 是的，我想我最大的感触是，我是这样看的。

sentences.en: Like, going into academia, like, as a student or as a faculty or whatever, as a research assistant or what have you, is a lot like owning your own business.
sentences.zh: 进入学术界，无论是作为学生、教职员工、研究助理还是其他什么身份，都非常像经营自己的生意。

sentences.en: Like, as a student, you're really in charge of your own fate more than you are as an employee.
sentences.zh: 作为学生，你对自己命运的掌控力比作为雇员时要大得多。

sentences.en: Like, as a student, you can very quickly, within a matter of three or four months, you can fail out of college, right?
sentences.zh: 作为学生，你可以在短短三四个月内就挂科退学，对吧？

sentences.en: But, you know, outside of, like, sexually harassing someone or something which is very unlikely, like, which would require, like, you to be a sociopath.
sentences.zh: 但是，除了性骚扰之类的情况（这非常罕见，除非你是反社会人格），

sentences.en: Like, outside of those crazy things, you'll almost never get fired within three to four months.
sentences.zh: 除了那些极端情况，你几乎不可能在三四个月内被解雇。

sentences.en: Like, for you to be fired, for most companies, for you to be fired for performance reasons,
sentences.zh: 对于大多数公司来说，如果你因为表现不佳而被解雇，

sentences.en: I mean, you have to actually be...
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，你必须真的……

sentences.en: It takes, like, 12 months.
sentences.zh: 这通常需要 12 个月的时间。

sentences.en: Yeah, you have to be messing up for a long time, right?
sentences.zh: 是的，你得搞砸很长一段时间，对吧？

sentences.en: I mean, you really have to be going down the wrong path and know it for a while.
sentences.zh: 你必须真的走上了错误的道路，并且自己也意识到了这一点。

sentences.en: But school, I mean, you could, you know, really just, like, you know, especially when you get
sentences.zh: 但在学校里，你可以……特别是在更高阶段，比如博士，甚至更糟，教授，如果你不写文章，

sentences.en: to the higher levels, like a PhD, or even worse, a professor, like, if you don't write, you know,
sentences.zh: 如果你没有足够的资助获批，没有足够的论文被录用，

sentences.en: if you don't get enough grants accepted, and you don't get enough papers accepted, you know,
sentences.zh: 虽然有些会议在寻找好的论文，但它们也非常挑剔。

sentences.en: there are people who want, you know, there are conferences that are looking for good papers, but they're also very selective.
sentences.zh: 如果你无法通过这些，你就拿不到经费，然后你不得不求着系里给你拨款，那结果通常很糟糕。

sentences.en: And if you don't get these things through, then you don't get funding, and then you have to kind of beg your department to float you, and that, you know, ends badly.
sentences.zh: 失败太容易了，就像经营自己的生意一样，职业生涯可能会被摧毁。

sentences.en: And it's so easy to fail, just like running your own business, and to just be destroyed in your career.
sentences.zh: 但另一方面，学术界给予你的是更多的自由。

sentences.en: But then on the flip side, what you're given in academia is a lot more freedom.
sentences.zh: 在学校里，你可以学习任何你想学的东西。

sentences.en: Like, in school, you can study whatever you want.
sentences.zh: 如果你想成为生物学家，你就可以成为生物学家，你可以研究任何东西。

sentences.en: You know, if you want to be a biologist, you'd be a biologist, you know, you study anything.
sentences.zh: 但如果你找了一份软件工程师的工作，那显然就受限多了，对吧？

sentences.en: But, you know, if you get a job as, say, a software engineer, then obviously it's much more limited, right?
sentences.zh: 所以这就是权衡所在。

sentences.en: So those are sort of the trade-offs.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我想我还能想到另外两点。

sentences.en: Well, there's, I guess I think about two other things.
sentences.zh: 第一，在学校里，几乎所有东西都是我们所谓的“绿地项目”（从零开始）。

sentences.en: One is that, like, in school, almost everything was whatever we call greenfield work.
sentences.zh: 一切都是全新的，对吧？

sentences.en: So, like, everything is completely unwritten, right?
sentences.zh: 你是从零开始写东西。

sentences.en: You're writing stuff from scratch.
sentences.zh: 而大多数时候，当你工作时，已经有现成的代码存在了。

sentences.en: And most of the time, when you're working on a job, there's already something that exists.
sentences.zh: 是的，确实如此。

sentences.en: Yeah, that's true.
sentences.zh: 可能只是需求文档，但这种情况很少见。

sentences.en: It might just be requirements, but it's very rare.
sentences.zh: 我大部分的编码时间都花在处理别人的代码、处理遗留代码上。

sentences.en: I mean, almost all of my time spent coding is working in other people's code, working in legacy code.
sentences.zh: 即使我在写新代码，它也必须与别人的代码相兼容，对吧？

sentences.en: You know, even when I'm writing new code, it has to fit in with other people's code, right?
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 学校里也有这种情况，但没那么多。

sentences.en: There is some of that in school, but it's, you know, not as much.
sentences.zh: 另一件事是工作的连续性。

sentences.en: And then the other thing is, like, the continuity of work.
sentences.zh: 你可能一直在做同一件事。

sentences.en: Like, you could be working on the same thing.
sentences.zh: 至少如果你在做研究生工作和研究，情况可能不同。

sentences.en: So, at least in, like, if you're doing graduate work and research, it's probably different.
sentences.zh: 但作为本科生，你做的是小项目，一个长项目通常也就持续一个学期。

sentences.en: But, like, an undergraduate, you know, you're doing little projects, but there's typically a long project would last a semester.
sentences.zh: 而且大多数时候，一个学期会有多个项目，对吧？

sentences.en: And most times, projects are multiple per semester, right?
sentences.zh: 在课堂上。

sentences.en: In a class.
sentences.zh: 而在工作中，你可能很容易在几年内都在做基本相同的事情，或者至少几个月。

sentences.en: And at work, like, you could easily be working on basically the same thing for years, you know, but easily, you know, months.
sentences.zh: 你每天晚上回家，第二天早上回来，做的还是前一天晚上的事。

sentences.en: And you just, every night you go home and you come back the next morning and you're doing the same thing you were, like, the night before.
sentences.zh: 你只是不断地重复，一遍又一遍，对吧？

sentences.en: And you just keep doing it over and over and over again, you know?
sentences.zh: 是的，没错。

sentences.en: Yeah, right.

sentences.en: Yeah, actually, there's this interesting TED Talk, and we'll link to it in the show notes.

sentences.en: But it's about what makes us feel good about our work, and the reason why I bring it up

sentences.en: is they did this experiment where you, they had a control group where they started off paying them $5 to build this Lego.
sentences.zh: 他们有一盒乐高，你必须拼出某个东西。

sentences.en: So, they had a box of Lego, and you had to build something.
sentences.zh: 我想是一个机器人之类的，他们有说明书。

sentences.en: I think it was, like, a robot or something, and they had the instructions.
sentences.zh: 拼好之后，他们把它放到一边，拿到另一个房间，然后给你一盒新的，让你再拼一个。

sentences.en: And after you built it, they, you know, put it aside, they took it to another room, and they gave you a new box and told you to build another one.
sentences.zh: 但这次报酬只有 4 美元。

sentences.en: But this time it was only for, I think it was, like, $4.
sentences.zh: 他们有一个幂函数，对吧？

sentences.en: And they had some kind of power function, right?
sentences.zh: 大多数人一直拼机器人，直到报酬降到 0.7 美元左右。

sentences.en: And so, most people, like, kept building the robots until it was down to, like, $0.70.
sentences.zh: 然后对于第二组人，让他们拼好机器人，然后当着他们的面把机器人拆了，让他们再拼一次。

sentences.en: Then for the second group of people, they had them build the robot, and then they destroyed the robot in front of them, like, disassembled it, and had them build it again.
sentences.zh: 第二组人只拼了一两次就说不干了。

sentences.en: And that second group, like, only built the robot once or twice, and then said they were done.
sentences.zh: 所以，读研有点像是在第二组，因为你做了很多工作，而且很多时候是独自完成的。

sentences.en: And so, like, grad school is a little bit like being in that second group, because you do a lot of work, a lot of it is alone.
sentences.zh: 即使是做教授，很多工作也确实是在你自己的世界里。

sentences.en: Even being a professor, you know, a lot of the work, you're really, like, in your own world.
sentences.zh: 虽然你有向你汇报的团队学生，但你确实是孤军奋战。

sentences.en: I mean, you have students who are part of your team who kind of report to you, but you're really on your own.
sentences.zh: 很多工作（这是我的观点，仅供参考）最终会被销毁。

sentences.en: And a lot of the work, this is my opinion, so take out the grain of salt, but a lot of that work kind of gets destroyed.
sentences.zh: 它进入了某篇研究论文，然后希望工业界有人能拿去应用它。

sentences.en: You know, it goes into some research paper, and then hopefully someone in industry picks it up and does something with it.
sentences.zh: 我觉得这很像是在第二组。

sentences.en: But I felt like there's a lot of that kind of being in that second group.
sentences.zh: 但当你进入工业界时，确实有时会感觉自己只是庞大机器中的一颗螺丝钉。

sentences.en: But when you are in industry, it's true that, like, you sometimes can feel like you're a cog in a much larger machine.
sentences.zh: 但另一方面，你确实是这台正在做一些了不起事情的庞大机器的一部分。

sentences.en: But on the flip side, it's like, yes, you're part of a larger machine that's doing something pretty amazing.
sentences.zh: 这就是我所看到的巨大权衡。

sentences.en: And so that's sort of, like, the big trade-off I see.

sentences.zh: 但我可以在同一个数据库中有另一个文档，它是JSON格式，但没有成绩。

sentences.en: That's something completely different because, for whatever reason.
sentences.zh: 因为某种原因，这完全是另一回事。

sentences.en: So, in the case of the document store, it's much looser.
sentences.zh: 所以，在文档存储的情况下，它要宽松得多。

sentences.en: And just through advances in the technology and also computation power growing, you know,
sentences.zh: 仅仅通过技术的进步和计算能力的增长，你知道，

sentences.en: we're able to have these more sophisticated database management systems that can do all the things we talked about, the validation, the indexing, the caching,
sentences.zh: 我们能够拥有这些更复杂的数据库管理系统，它们可以完成我们谈到的所有事情，比如验证、索引、缓存，

sentences.en: without having such a tight schema as we do with SQL.
sentences.zh: 而不需要像SQL那样有严格的模式。

sentences.en: So, even with such a loose schema as you have in a document store, you know, given the right kind of resources and things like that,
sentences.zh: 所以，即使文档存储的模式很宽松，只要有合适的资源，

sentences.en: you can still do a lot of the things that we said at the beginning.
sentences.zh: 你仍然可以做我们开头提到的很多事情。

sentences.en: All right.
sentences.zh: 好了。

sentences.en: So, now, quickly, as, like, an overcap, you know, we'll talk about, because you may be thinking of a given database and, like, oh, I wonder what it is.
sentences.zh: 现在，快速总结一下，因为你可能在想某个特定的数据库，想知道它属于哪种。

sentences.en: Or maybe we just mentioned some databases you might be interested in looking up.
sentences.zh: 或者我们刚才提到的某些数据库你可能想去查一查。

sentences.en: We're going to kind of go through some breakdown of the various implementations of the databases and some examples, if we can give, and what kind they are.
sentences.zh: 我们将对各种数据库的实现进行一些拆解，尽可能给出一些例子，并说明它们属于哪种类型。

sentences.en: So, first kind of section is the lightweight, embedded, you know, probably only runs on one computer database.
sentences.zh: 第一类是轻量级的、嵌入式的，通常只在一台计算机上运行的数据库。

sentences.en: And the first example that is very popular is SQLite, S-Q-L-I-T-E, SQLite.
sentences.zh: 第一个非常流行的例子是SQLite，S-Q-L-I-T-E，SQLite。

sentences.en: And it is a SQL implementation, a relational database, but it can be even embedded in your program and is super simple to use.
sentences.zh: 它是一个SQL实现，一个关系型数据库，但它可以嵌入到你的程序中，使用起来超级简单。

sentences.en: And, you know, kind of one of those things, if you get, start to get any sort of complicated data you're trying to store in your program, you should consider using this instead,
sentences.zh: 如果你开始在程序中存储任何复杂的数据，你应该考虑使用它，

sentences.en: because it may make your life, you know, easier.
sentences.zh: 因为它可能会让你的生活更轻松。

sentences.en: And it's quite efficient.
sentences.zh: 而且它非常高效。

sentences.en: It doesn't take, you don't have to run a separate server and connect to it.
sentences.zh: 你不需要运行一个单独的服务器并连接到它。

sentences.en: It kind of reduces the complexity of that that's necessary.
sentences.zh: 它减少了所需的复杂性。

sentences.en: Yeah, I mean, I think it's even built into some languages.
sentences.zh: 我觉得它甚至内置在一些语言中。

sentences.en: Like, I know Python has SQLite built in.
sentences.zh: 比如我知道Python就内置了SQLite。

sentences.en: I didn't know that.
sentences.zh: 我之前不知道。

sentences.en: So, yeah, I mean, you don't even, you really don't have to do a lot of work to get it up and running.
sentences.zh: 所以，你真的不需要做太多工作就能让它运行起来。

sentences.en: And I know Jason's used Berkeley DB for stuff, right?
sentences.zh: 我知道Jason用过Berkeley DB，对吧？

sentences.en: I think you were talking about it.
sentences.zh: 我想你之前提到过。

sentences.en: Yeah, yeah, Berkeley DB is pretty cool.
sentences.zh: 是的，Berkeley DB确实很酷。

sentences.en: Actually, I'll list another one on here, MapDB.
sentences.zh: 其实我还要列出另一个，MapDB。

sentences.en: And so these are also embedded.
sentences.zh: 这些也是嵌入式的。

sentences.en: So as Patrick was saying, you know, let's say you have some program that you're writing and you need to store some kind of configuration.
sentences.zh: 正如Patrick所说，假设你正在编写一个程序，需要存储某种配置。

sentences.en: Like, do people, you know, what sounds do people want when they log in?
sentences.zh: 比如，人们登录时想要什么样的声音？

sentences.en: Or, you know, it's some kind of music app, you know, or sorry, some kind of, like, music creation program.
sentences.zh: 或者这是一个音乐应用，或者某种音乐创作程序。

sentences.en: You know, what settings do they want their piano set at?
sentences.zh: 他们希望钢琴设置成什么样？

sentences.en: You know, these kind of configuration things.
sentences.zh: 这些配置类的数据。

sentences.en: These embedded databases are great for that because you could just load it from a file, store it to a file.
sentences.zh: 这些嵌入式数据库非常适合，因为你可以直接从文件加载，保存到文件。

sentences.en: It could be part of your program.
sentences.zh: 它可以是你程序的一部分。

sentences.en: You don't have to go phone home or something like that, you know, contact a server or anything.
sentences.zh: 你不需要去连接服务器之类的。

sentences.en: So SQLite is a relational database.
sentences.zh: 所以SQLite是一个关系型数据库。

sentences.en: So, you know, it uses SQL with the structure tables and things like that.
sentences.zh: 它使用带有结构化表等的SQL。

sentences.en: If you just want a key value store, so, again, like, you give it, you look up a key, you get a value.
sentences.zh: 如果你只是想要一个键值存储，即通过键查找值，

sentences.en: Then you can use BerkeleyDB or MapDB.
sentences.zh: 那么你可以使用BerkeleyDB或MapDB。

sentences.en: BerkeleyDB is written in C++, but there are bindings for a bunch of different languages.
sentences.zh: BerkeleyDB是用C++编写的，但有许多不同语言的绑定。

sentences.en: MapDB is a lot better, but it's written in Java.
sentences.zh: MapDB好得多，但它是用Java编写的。

sentences.en: So if, you know, the quick answer is if you're using Java, use MapDB.
sentences.zh: 所以简单的回答是：如果你用Java，就用MapDB。

sentences.en: If you're using any other language, use BerkeleyDB.
sentences.zh: 如果你用其他语言，就用BerkeleyDB。

sentences.en: Next, we move up the scale to something that you would probably be running on a server.
sentences.zh: 接下来，我们升级到通常在服务器上运行的数据库。

sentences.en: But if you wanted something really fast and, you know, your data size was kept under control, but you wanted it to run in memory, you get to your next set of databases.
sentences.zh: 但如果你想要非常快，且数据量可控，又希望在内存中运行，那就到了下一类数据库。

sentences.en: The one that you see all the time on, like, Hacker News and other websites is Redis.
sentences.zh: 你在Hacker News和其他网站上经常看到的一个是Redis。

sentences.en: Is that how you say it?
sentences.zh: 是这样读的吗？

sentences.en: I actually don't know.
sentences.zh: 我其实不知道。

sentences.en: I think so.
sentences.zh: 我想是吧。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好吧。

sentences.en: It's like all these names.
sentences.zh: 这些名字真是五花八门。

sentences.en: I only ever read them.
sentences.zh: 我只读过它们，没听过。

sentences.en: Actually, I just happened to, just total coincidence, I went to a Redis meetup, and it is Redis.
sentences.zh: 其实我刚好去过一个Redis聚会，确实读作Redis。

sentences.en: At least the people there all said Redis.
sentences.zh: 至少那里的人都读Redis。

sentences.en: All right.
sentences.zh: 好吧。

sentences.en: So, yep, Redis.
sentences.zh: 所以，没错，Redis。

sentences.en: And that's a key value store.
sentences.zh: 它是一个键值存储。

sentences.en: So, it's gaining a lot of popularity recently.
sentences.zh: 最近非常流行。

sentences.en: It's pretty lightweight, and it's really fast if your data size is, you know, in the range that you can hold in main memory.
sentences.zh: 它很轻量，如果你的数据量在内存能容纳的范围内，它非常快。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Keep in mind, like, once you shut down Redis, or even, like, periodically, it saves to disk.
sentences.zh: 记住，一旦你关闭Redis，或者定期地，它会保存到磁盘。

sentences.en: So, it's not like, it's not truly in memory where, you know, you shut down the computer and you lose everything.
sentences.zh: 所以它不是那种真正的内存数据库，关机就什么都没了。

sentences.en: But the idea is, yeah, at any given time, all of the data is in memory.
sentences.zh: 但理念是，在任何给定时间，所有数据都在内存中。

sentences.en: Yep.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Another one is memcached D.
sentences.zh: 另一个是memcached。

sentences.en: I think that's how you say it.
sentences.zh: 我想是这样读的。

sentences.en: Or do you just say memcached?
sentences.zh: 还是直接读memcached？

sentences.en: I've heard it.
sentences.zh: 我听过这种说法。

sentences.en: I say memcached.
sentences.zh: 我读memcached。

sentences.en: Really?
sentences.zh: 真的吗？

sentences.en: I heard people say memcached D, but okay.
sentences.zh: 我听过有人读memcached D，不过好吧。

sentences.en: It could be.
sentences.zh: 也可能是那样。

sentences.en: I mean, I actually have, I've only said it.
sentences.zh: 我其实只读过它。

sentences.en: I've never heard anyone else say it now that I think about it.
sentences.zh: 仔细想想，我从来没听过别人怎么读。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好吧。

sentences.en: So, I don't know.
sentences.zh: 所以我不知道。

sentences.en: This is another one you hear, and this is often when you hear about somebody's having a performance
sentences.zh: 这是另一个你常听到的名字，通常是在有人遇到性能问题时，

sentences.en: problem with their SQL database, right?
sentences.zh: SQL数据库出现问题时，对吧？

sentences.en: We'll talk about some in a second.
sentences.zh: 我们一会儿再谈。

sentences.en: But, you know, they're having problems because there's some specific data that it just has
sentences.zh: 他们遇到问题是因为某些特定数据的访问频率很高，

sentences.en: a higher access rate or different pattern than what, you know, SQL stuff was built to handle.
sentences.zh: 或者访问模式与SQL数据库的设计初衷不同。

sentences.en: And you'll hear about people talking about this as a way to store data in memory and be,
sentences.zh: 你会听到人们谈论用它作为内存存储数据的方式，

sentences.en: have very fast access times and kind of alleviate some of the slowness that can happen if you have too many concurrent users to a SQL database.
sentences.zh: 以获得极快的访问速度，缓解SQL数据库在并发用户过多时可能出现的缓慢问题。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Like, in contrast with Redis, memcached, when you shut down the machine, it does destroy the database.
sentences.zh: 与Redis不同，memcached在机器关闭时会销毁数据库。

sentences.en: So, the idea with memcached, as Patrick was saying, is to use to augment another database.
sentences.zh: 所以，正如Patrick所说，memcached的理念是用来增强另一个数据库。

sentences.en: And it's for when that database is too slow.
sentences.zh: 它是为了解决那个数据库太慢的问题。

sentences.en: So, you can imagine, like, things that would be good for memcached should be, you know, the front page of your website, you know, things like that.
sentences.zh: 你可以想象，适合用memcached的东西应该是网站首页之类的。

sentences.en: And there's a lot of, you know, if you use, like, Ruby on Rails or if you use, you know,
sentences.zh: 如果你使用Ruby on Rails，或者使用很多内容管理系统，

sentences.en: a lot of these, like, content management systems, you know, most of them will support memcached.
sentences.zh: 它们大多数都支持memcached。

sentences.en: And they will, you know, things like the front page of your website, they will put in main memory.
sentences.zh: 它们会把网站首页之类的内容放在主内存中。

sentences.en: So, I have no idea why I've heard people say memcached before, because it looks like it's just memcached.
sentences.zh: 我完全不知道为什么我之前听过别人读memcached，因为它看起来就是memcached。

sentences.en: You're right.
sentences.zh: 你说得对。

sentences.en: Oh, did you actually find a pronunciation?
sentences.zh: 哦，你真的查到发音了吗？

sentences.en: So, well, I was trying to look for it.
sentences.zh: 我试着查了一下。

sentences.en: So, I see other people saying that they hear it as memcached.
sentences.zh: 我看到其他人说他们听到的读法是memcached。

sentences.en: Memcached, I don't know.
sentences.zh: Memcached，我不知道。

sentences.en: I can't find a definitive answer.
sentences.zh: 我找不到确切的答案。

sentences.en: I think, you know, so memcached makes the most sense, because I think it's a memcached daemon.
sentences.zh: 我觉得memcached最合理，因为我觉得它是memcached daemon（守护进程）。

sentences.en: I think that's where the name comes from.
sentences.zh: 我觉得名字就是这么来的。

sentences.en: But I just, I don't know.
sentences.zh: 但我真的不知道。

sentences.en: I mean, just because it makes sense, it doesn't mean it's right.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，仅仅因为它合理，并不代表它是对的。

sentences.en: So, it's kind of silly, but I remember when Linux was first kind of, well, when I first started encountering it, and nobody knew exactly how to say it, like, none of my friends.
sentences.zh: 这有点傻，但我记得Linux刚出现时，或者我刚接触它时，没人知道怎么读，我的朋友们都不知道。

sentences.en: And, this is before YouTube videos, I guess, so you couldn't look on YouTube videos for how to say it.
sentences.zh: 而且，我想这还是在 YouTube 视频出现之前的事，所以你没法在 YouTube 视频上查到该怎么读。

sentences.en: Yeah, I remember when people called it Linux.
sentences.zh: 是啊，我记得以前有人管它叫 Linux。

sentences.en: Yeah, right, exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错，确实是这样。

sentences.en: Linux, Linux, Linux.
sentences.zh: Linux，Linux，Linux。

sentences.en: It's like people would say weird stuff.
sentences.zh: 就好像人们会说些奇怪的东西一样。

sentences.en: I've never heard that one.
sentences.zh: 我从没听说过那个读法。

sentences.en: Yeah, I heard all sorts of strange things.
sentences.zh: 是啊，我听过各种各样奇怪的说法。

sentences.en: Linux.
sentences.zh: Linux。

sentences.en: But now, I guess, there's so much video, right?
sentences.zh: 但现在，我想，视频资源太多了，对吧？

sentences.en: Like, I don't know what exactly happened, but I've never heard people say anything other than Linux anymore.
sentences.zh: 我不知道具体发生了什么，但我再也没听过人们说 Linux 以外的其他读法了。

sentences.en: Yeah, that's a good point.
sentences.zh: 没错，说得好。

sentences.en: I'm not sure what caused the transition.
sentences.zh: 我不确定是什么导致了这种转变。

sentences.en: Maybe it is, you know.
sentences.zh: 也许就是这样吧，你知道的。

sentences.en: Maybe, that would be really interesting if YouTube, like, homogenized, you know, language.
sentences.zh: 也许吧，如果 YouTube 真的能让语言趋于统一，那会非常有趣。

sentences.en: That would be, like, something really interesting to study.
sentences.zh: 那确实是一个非常值得研究的课题。

sentences.en: I'm sure some linguist is looking into that right now.
sentences.zh: 我相信肯定有语言学家正在研究这个问题。

sentences.en: Using disk-based server databases.
sentences.zh: 使用基于磁盘的服务器数据库。

sentences.en: Yeah, that's right.
sentences.zh: 是的，没错。

sentences.en: So, the most obvious, you know, first ones you think about are MySQL, SQL Server, Postgres.
sentences.zh: 所以，你最先想到的、最显而易见的那些，就是 MySQL、SQL Server 和 Postgres。

sentences.en: You know, these are ones that a lot of people have heard of.
sentences.zh: 你知道，这些都是很多人听说过的。

sentences.en: They've been around for a long time.
sentences.zh: 它们已经存在很长时间了。

sentences.en: They're some free, some paid, some varying licenses.
sentences.zh: 有些是免费的，有些是付费的，还有各种不同的授权协议。

sentences.en: Yeah, can you explain?
sentences.zh: 是啊，你能解释一下吗？

sentences.en: Do you understand the MySQL license?
sentences.zh: 你了解 MySQL 的授权协议吗？

sentences.en: No, I don't understand.
sentences.zh: 不，我不了解。

sentences.en: No, no.
sentences.zh: 不，不。

sentences.en: Don't ask me about any of that.
sentences.zh: 别问我这些。

sentences.en: I have no idea.
sentences.zh: 我完全没头绪。

sentences.en: I mean, it looks to me like if you use the MySQL, you know, client, even the client, then you have to pay them money.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，在我看来，如果你使用了 MySQL 的客户端，哪怕只是客户端，你就得付钱给他们。

sentences.en: That's how I read it.
sentences.zh: 我是这么理解的。

sentences.en: But that can't be true, so I don't know.
sentences.zh: 但这不可能，所以我也不清楚。

sentences.en: There are people's whole jobs who are, like, around optimizing and selecting what the differences are between the different databases.
sentences.zh: 有些人专门以此为业，就是围绕着如何优化以及如何选择不同数据库之间的差异。

sentences.en: I'm not that person.
sentences.zh: 我不是那种人。

sentences.en: I appreciate those people, but I'm not that person.
sentences.zh: 我很敬佩那些人，但我不是。

sentences.en: Yeah, definitely.
sentences.zh: 是的，绝对是。

sentences.en: There's a whole art to making MySQL run the way you want it to, given your data.
sentences.zh: 要让 MySQL 根据你的数据按你想要的方式运行，这本身就是一门艺术。

sentences.en: And Patrick and I are very happy to let people much more qualified than we are do that.
sentences.zh: Patrick 和我非常乐意让比我们更有资格的人去做这些事。

sentences.en: That is true.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: Yeah, so those are in the SQL family.
sentences.zh: 好的，这些属于 SQL 家族。

sentences.en: If you're interested in the column family, which, again, just a reminder, that's the key value where there could be multiple values, right?
sentences.zh: 如果你对列族（Column Family）感兴趣，再次提醒一下，那就是键值对中可能存在多个值的情况，对吧？

sentences.en: So, you know, column family, if you have just one column in the column family, then you have a key value database.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，列族，如果你在列族中只有一个列，那你拥有的就是一个键值数据库。

sentences.en: So think of the column family as being a superset of what a key value database can do.
sentences.zh: 所以，把列族看作是键值数据库功能的超集。

sentences.en: So, in that category, there's two big ones.
sentences.zh: 在这一类别中，有两个大头。

sentences.en: One is Cassandra, and the other is HBase.
sentences.zh: 一个是 Cassandra，另一个是 HBase。

sentences.en: The short story is, the reason why there's two, they use kind of different technologies for scaling.
sentences.zh: 简单来说，之所以有两个，是因为它们在扩展时使用了不同的技术。

sentences.en: So, in other words, when you have to split the, to shard the database among, say, 10 or 100 computers, both each of those two, HBase and Cassandra, handle that differently.
sentences.zh: 换句话说，当你需要拆分数据库，或者说在 10 台或 100 台计算机之间进行分片时，HBase 和 Cassandra 处理的方式各不相同。

sentences.en: And let's just say the tradeoff there is, you know, Cassandra is easier to set up.
sentences.zh: 我们只能说，其中的权衡在于，Cassandra 更容易设置。

sentences.en: Definitely, if you're running on one machine, Cassandra is way easier to set up.
sentences.zh: 绝对是这样，如果你是在单机上运行，Cassandra 的设置要容易得多。

sentences.en: But even as you scale out, the setup and the maintenance is pretty easy.
sentences.zh: 即使在你进行横向扩展时，设置和维护也相当简单。

sentences.en: But on the flip side, if you do have performance issues, it can be kind of a nightmare.
sentences.zh: 但另一方面，如果你遇到了性能问题，那可能会是一场噩梦。

sentences.en: That's just been my experience.
sentences.zh: 这只是我的个人经验。

sentences.en: HBase is harder to set up.
sentences.zh: HBase 设置起来比较困难。

sentences.en: So, it actually requires a lot of Apache libraries and services that you have to install manually, like ZooKeeper.
sentences.zh: 它实际上需要很多 Apache 的库和服务，你必须手动安装，比如 ZooKeeper。

sentences.en: So, you actually have to, you know, install ZooKeeper, start a ZooKeeper server, and then install HBase and install and get an HBase server.
sentences.zh: 所以，你实际上必须安装 ZooKeeper，启动一个 ZooKeeper 服务器，然后安装 HBase，并获取一个 HBase 服务器。

sentences.en: So, this is actually two servers.
sentences.zh: 所以，这实际上是两个服务器。

sentences.en: So, it's got overhead, but on the flip side, it just seems like tuning and understanding what's going on is a lot easier with HBase.
sentences.zh: 因此，它有额外的开销，但另一方面，使用 HBase 进行调优和理解其运行机制似乎要容易得多。

sentences.en: So, that's column family.
sentences.zh: 这就是列族数据库。

sentences.en: And then for document store, there's also a bunch of them.
sentences.zh: 至于文档存储，也有很多选择。

sentences.en: My favorite is MongoDB.
sentences.zh: 我最喜欢的是 MongoDB。

sentences.en: I really think MongoDB is very clever in their API.
sentences.zh: 我真的认为 MongoDB 的 API 非常巧妙。

sentences.en: I'm a big fan.
sentences.zh: 我是它的忠实粉丝。

sentences.en: I felt like, so they have this kind of cool sort of REST-based JSON API.
sentences.zh: 我觉得他们有一种很酷的、基于 REST 的 JSON API。

sentences.en: They also have a good Java API.
sentences.zh: 他们也有很好的 Java API。

sentences.en: They are now, they've recently added full text indexing, which is pretty cool.
sentences.zh: 他们最近还增加了全文索引功能，这非常酷。

sentences.en: So, you can actually say this column, you know, if I want to be able to do, like, fuzzy text searches on this column.
sentences.zh: 所以，你可以指定这一列，比如，如果你想对这一列进行模糊文本搜索。

sentences.en: You can just annotate the column, and boom, you get fuzzy text searches.
sentences.zh: 你只需要给这一列加上注解，砰，你就能实现模糊文本搜索了。

sentences.en: So, just to recap, like, if the column was, you know, say, a web page.
sentences.zh: 所以，简单回顾一下，如果这一列是，比如说，一个网页。

sentences.en: Let's say one column of your database or one document of your database is a website.
sentences.zh: 假设你数据库中的一列或一个文档是一个网站。

sentences.en: All of the XML or all of the HTML for a website.
sentences.zh: 包含了网站所有的 XML 或 HTML。

sentences.en: You could just turn on this full text indexing, and now you have a search engine over the whole web.
sentences.zh: 你只需要开启这个全文索引，现在你就拥有了一个覆盖整个网站的搜索引擎。

sentences.en: Now, of course, you know, I mean, it's probably not optimized for that much data, but you get the idea.
sentences.zh: 当然，我的意思是，它可能没有针对那么大的数据量进行优化，但你明白我的意思。

sentences.en: It's still pretty powerful.
sentences.zh: 它依然非常强大。

sentences.en: If you're building your own wiki or something like that, it's pretty cool to kind of get full text searching for free.
sentences.zh: 如果你正在构建自己的维基百科之类的东西，能免费获得全文搜索功能真的很酷。

sentences.en: There's also RethinkDB, which we talked about at the beginning of the show.
sentences.zh: 还有 RethinkDB，我们在节目开头提到过它。

sentences.en: So, they're definitely, like, new guys on the block, so, you know, they are kind of iterating very quickly.
sentences.zh: 他们绝对是这个领域的新人，所以，你知道，他们迭代得非常快。

sentences.en: And, you know, I think it'll be pretty cool, but we'll have to sort of wait and see, you know, what they come out with in the future.
sentences.zh: 而且，我觉得这会很酷，但我们还得拭目以待，看看他们未来会推出什么。

sentences.en: It's still kind of early.
sentences.zh: 现在还处于早期阶段。

sentences.en: All right.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: Well, that about wraps it up.
sentences.zh: 好吧，节目差不多到这里就结束了。

sentences.en: So, I'm hoping that we didn't repeat too much of what we said when we did query languages, but that was, like, a long time ago.
sentences.zh: 我希望我们没有过多重复我们在讲查询语言时说过的内容，但那已经是很久以前的事了。

sentences.en: It's, like, 14 episodes ago.
sentences.zh: 那是 14 期节目之前的事了。

sentences.en: So, hopefully, there's not too much of a repeat.
sentences.zh: 所以，希望不会有太多的重复。

sentences.en: And thank you guys for all your emails.
sentences.zh: 感谢大家的来信。

sentences.en: Get lots of on our Google Plus page or community.
sentences.zh: 在我们的 Google Plus 页面或社区上收到了很多反馈。

sentences.en: I guess it's a community now.
sentences.zh: 我想现在它算是一个社区了。

sentences.en: People post on there, and that's cool.
sentences.zh: 人们在那上面发帖，这很酷。

sentences.en: We see them.
sentences.zh: 我们都看到了。

sentences.en: Even if we don't respond, we do see them, and emails to us are always appreciated.
sentences.zh: 即使我们没有回复，我们也确实看到了，我们一直很感激发给我们的邮件。

sentences.en: Yeah, thanks, Ash, for your question.
sentences.zh: 是的，谢谢 Ash 提出的问题。

sentences.en: That kind of got the whole episode kicked off.
sentences.zh: 这算是开启了整期节目。

sentences.en: So, yeah, definitely, you know, post on the community if you have any questions or any feedback or anything like that.
sentences.zh: 所以，没错，如果你有任何问题、反馈或类似的事情，一定要在社区里发帖。

sentences.en: We do read it, and it does give us a lot of inspiration for the show and things like that.
sentences.zh: 我们确实会阅读，这为我们的节目提供了很多灵感之类的东西。

sentences.en: But we will definitely do Swift as a next episode.
sentences.zh: 但我们下一期一定会做 Swift。

sentences.en: We'll have to beef up on our Swift between now and then.
sentences.zh: 在这之前，我们得好好补补 Swift 的知识。

sentences.en: But, yeah, I'm looking forward to that one.
sentences.zh: 不过，我真的很期待那一期。

sentences.en: Cool.
sentences.zh: 酷。

sentences.en: I think that's a wrap.
sentences.zh: 我想节目就到这里了。

sentences.en: All right, cool.
sentences.zh: 好的，酷。

sentences.en: See you guys in a couple of weeks.
sentences.zh: 几周后再见。
